regions.name: Cornwall
regions.description: The UK's surf capital. Atlantic-facing beaches on the north coast pick up almost every swell, while the south coast lights up in big winter storms.

regions.name: Devon
regions.description: North Devon's long, west-facing beaches catch Atlantic groundswell, and the south coast's river mouths come alive in large south-westerly swells.

regions.name: Dorset
regions.description: Channel surf that needs a solid south-westerly swell. Expect fun beach peaks in Bournemouth and quality reef breaks along the Jurassic Coast.

regions.name: South Wales
regions.description: Consistent Bristol Channel and Atlantic surf from the wide-open beaches of Pembrokeshire's south coast to Porthcawl.

regions.name: Gower
regions.description: Britain's first Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, with south-facing bays that turn on in large south-westerly swells and northerly winds.

regions.name: Pembrokeshire
regions.description: St Brides Bay and St Davids catch Atlantic swell from the west and south-west, with easterly winds blowing offshore.

regions.name: North Wales
regions.description: Fickle but rewarding. The Llŷn Peninsula and Anglesey need a south-westerly swell and easterly winds to fire.

regions.name: Yorkshire
regions.description: North Sea surf with reefs, points and beach breaks that come alive in northerly swells and south-westerly winds.

regions.name: North East
regions.description: Tyneside's sheltered bays turn on with North Sea swell from the north-east and westerly offshore winds.

regions.name: Scotland
regions.description: World-class reefs on the north coast, East Lothian beaches in North Sea swell and the exposed Atlantic west coast of Kintyre.

regions.name: Northern Ireland
regions.description: The Causeway Coast's long sandy beaches catch North Atlantic swell, with southerly winds blowing offshore.
